newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank, Bonn found "common way" on gold - Waigel.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank, Bonn found "common way" on gold - Waigel.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday the German government and the Bundesbank had reached a common language and way of proceeding on a planned revaluation of central bank assets.
"We have found a common way," Waigel told the Bundestag lower house of parliament in a government statement on his proposals for revaluing gold reserves to help plug budget gaps.
Waigel also said that he and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer would do their best to have windfall funds created by the revaluation transfered to Bonn from 1998 and not earlier.
He said the Finance Ministry and the Bundesbank were discussing the details of such an asset and they would make sure it would not have any damaging affect on money supply or lead to inflation.

Waigel was addressing parliament to explain government plans to revalue Bundesbank assets a day after Bonn retreated on its original plan to release funds created by the plan in 1997 to help Germany qualify for European monetary union (EMU).
Opposition Social Democrats and Greens tabled a motion calling for Waigel's resignation over the crisis and Bundestag members were due to vote on it after a debate on the gold plan.
